newsitem.title: ITALY: Arafat urges Israeli flexibility in future talks.
newsitem.headline: Arafat urges Israeli flexibility in future talks.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat urged Israel on Tuesday to be flexible in future talks on a lasting settlement between Arabs and Jews.

"The peace we are looking for...will face many risks and threats," Arafat told a congress of the Socialist International on his first trip since taking over most of the West Bank city of Hebron at the weekend in a landmark deal with Israel.

Arafat, using his speech to anticipate future talks, said obstacles included "attempts to impose de-facto policies from one side on a number of major issues to be discussed at the final status negotiations".
The fate of the Jews in Hebron and other West Bank settlements is due to be decided in "final status" talks between Israel and the Palestinian Authority scheduled to be completed by May 1999.

Arafat said other risks were "the support to settlement activities all over the Palestinian territories, particularly in Holy Jerusalem, al-Quds, the ongoing closure (of Israel's borders with areas of Palestinian self-rule) policy (and) the economic siege".
The long-delayed Hebron deal, the first between Arafat and right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, was signed after months of negotiations and arm-twisting by the United States.

It hands over most of Hebron to Palestinian rule after 30 years of occupation but leaves Israel in charge of one-fifth of the town where 400 Jewish settlers and 20,000 Arabs live, plus the Tomb of the Patriarchs, a site holy to Moslems and Jews.

Arafat, taking control of the town last Sunday, made clear he saw the deal as a stepping stone to the establishment of a Palestinian state and repeated his promise to make Arab East Jerusalem his capital.
Asked by reporters after the speech whether he thought the Hebron deal would facilitate futher talks, he said: "I hope so. There is no doubt it is a very important step".

He told the congress that he hoped the Hebron deal would be implemented "accurately and honestly, in particular regarding the redeployment from more Palestinian land, in accordance with the designated dates and timetable, which is to say no later than the middle of next year".
He also urged wider Middle East peace efforts.

"We are looking forward to achieve comprehensive peace in the Middle East and we need your efforts, and the efforts of all those who believe in this peace process, to move it ahead on the Syrian and Lebanese tracks," he told the congress.

Former Israeli prime minister Shimon Peres also told the Socialist International, which brings together 139 left-wing parties and organisations from around the world, that negotiations with Syria were unavoidable.
"We cannot have a connection of separate islands of peace. The Middle East must become a continent of peace where evil storms will not be able to come in," he said.
"Like it or not, we must negotiate with the Syrians and President Assad."
Peres said he was glad the Hebron deal had been reached but said a long list of difficult decisions remained, including the on-schedule redeployment of troops in the West Bank.
"We have to reach a permanent solution with the Palestinians...as soon as we can, before the end of the century," he said.
